conversation.content:
Hello there. I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Dr. Patel, and I’m the perinatal mental-health clinician who works with new mothers in our practice. I’d like to spend a few minutes with you using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS—to see how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived.

This is simply a screening tool: ten short questions about the past seven days that help us catch anything from normal “baby blues” to signs of depression or anxiety that deserve extra support. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays confidential within our team. If at any point you feel uncomfortable, we can pause or stop—this is your space.

I’ll ask each question conversationally; just tell me what feels closest to your experience and we’ll move on. Ready to begin?

Over the past week, when you were able to laugh and see the funny side of things, how did that feel for you?

Honestly, I haven’t really felt much like laughing. When my partner or the sitcom we usually watch tries to be funny, I give a polite little chuckle, but it feels forced. It’s like the joy is stuck behind a wall—I can see that something is supposed to be amusing, but I don’t feel it in my chest the way I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I can manage a small laugh here or there, but it feels kind of flat—like I’m going through the motions rather than actually finding things funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I used to get excited about little plans—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park, even just a quiet shower—but lately it feels like nothing sounds worth the effort. I’ll think, “That might be nice,” and then it just seems exhausting. So, no, I haven’t really looked forward to anything with actual enjoyment this week.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. When the baby wouldn’t settle last night, I kept thinking it must be because I’m not doing something right—like I’m failing him somehow. Even little things, like forgetting to bring a burp cloth, turn into this loop of “I’m a terrible mom.” I know in my head it’s not logical, but the guilt just pops up anyway.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much yes. My mind keeps spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby—Is he breathing? Is that rash normal? Am I producing enough milk?—even when everything checks out fine at the pediatrician’s. It’s like I can’t shut the worry off, even when there’s no real reason to be alarmed.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes, that happens. A couple of times this week I’ll just be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my heart starts racing and I feel shaky, like something awful is about to happen—even though nothing’s wrong. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days it feels like I’m drowning in small tasks. The dishes pile up, the baby needs holding, I’m running on no real sleep, and I keep thinking, “I can’t keep up.” I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m barely treading water and waiting for the next wave to hit.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head just keeps spinning with worries and this heavy, sad feeling. Some nights I drift off okay, then jolt awake for the next feed and can’t get back to sleep even after he’s settled. It’s like the unhappiness sits on my chest and won’t let me rest.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the week, that’s how I’ve felt. It’s like a gray cloud is just parked over me—I wake up already heavy, and it lingers all day. I wouldn’t say every single moment, but definitely the majority of the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes, a few times. Mostly when everything feels like too much—like yesterday when the baby wouldn’t nap and I couldn’t get the sling adjusted. I just sat on the couch and cried for a few minutes, then felt silly for crying over something so small.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel low and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms:  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, frequent tearfulness  
- Marked guilt/self-blame (“terrible mom” cognitions)  
- Generalized anxiety, intrusive “what-ifs,” nocturnal rumination  
- Discrete panic episodes (racing heart, trembling) without clear trigger  
- Overwhelm with daily tasks, “drowning” sensation  
- Sleep disruption: initial insomnia and inability to return to sleep post-feedings, mood-driven  
- Crying spells when frustrated; affect flat or sad most days  

Observed patterns:  
Consistent dysphoria and loss of enjoyment across the full week; anxiety symptoms co-occur and intensify at night. Functional impact: difficulty completing household tasks and self-care; still managing infant’s basic needs.

Risk indicators:  
- Depressed mood plus anhedonia  
- Excessive guilt / feelings of inadequacy  
- Mood-related insomnia  
- Recurrent panic-like episodes  
- Denies self-harm ideation (no safety concern at present)

Screening impression:  
High clinical concern for postpartum major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety features; warrants formal assessment (PHQ-9/EPDS) and prompt referral to perinatal mental health specialist for evaluation and possible intervention.
